# npu: generation prompt

*Generated by `ip/scripts/make_ip_prompts.py` from the RTL and testbench sources on 2026-10-26. It follows `ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md`; edit any field before use.*

```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `npu_top` (IP directory `npu`)
- Library category: `ai`
- Location: `ip/ai/npu/`
- One-line purpose: INT8 neural-network accelerator (golden model: model/npu_model.py, NpuTop; every operation's DDR result equals the model's bit for bit, the RTL's timing is its own).
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: `video_processor`.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate):

| Module | From | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axil_if` | `shared/src` | AXI4-Lite interface of the FPGA Cores 4 U library, the common definition every block's register-bus ports follow. |
| `regbus_if` | `shared/src` | Simple register bus between an AXI4-Lite front end (axi4_lite_slave, axil_regbus) and the register block: one-clock write / read strobes, error answers that become SLVERR. |
| `axis_if` | `shared/src` | AXI4-Stream interface of the FPGA Cores 4 U library, the common definition every block's stream ports follow. |
| `axi4_lite_slave` | `axi4_lite_slave` | Generic AXI4-Lite slave front end. |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning / legal range |
|---|---|---|
| `ADDR_W` | `32` | AXI byte address bits |
| `ID_W` | `4` | AXI ID bits |
| `PE_P` | `64` | MAC array: output pixels per strip |
| `PE_O` | `64` | MAC array: output channels per tile |

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil** - interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`), ADDR_W = 8.
- **s_axis** - interface `axis_if.monitor` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`), DATA_W = 24.
- **m_axi_*** - AXI4 (full) master, address [ADDR_W-1:0], data [255:0]: discrete ports (bursts and IDs; the library has no full-AXI4 interface).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Declare bus ports as interface ports (`axis_if.slave s_axis`) with the interface, modport and parameters in a comment line directly above: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Widths are module parameters (Icarus has no $bits of an interface member); connect `.p(inst)`, not `.p(inst.mp)`. Yosys reads a top with interface ports through its discrete wrapper (`ip/scripts/syn_wrap.py`, sv2v); cocotb tests drive such a wrapper's plain ports.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | clock |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | synchronous, active low |
| `irq_o` | output | 1 | s_axil: axil_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv), ADDR_W = 8 | - | IRQ_STATUS & IRQ_EN |
| `run_done_o` | output | 1 | s_axil: axil_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv), ADDR_W = 8 | - | one clock: a run has finished (IRQ_STATUS[0] set) |
| `auto_o` | output | 1 | s_axil: axil_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv), ADDR_W = 8 | - | CTRL.EN, AUTO and WRITE: a run follows every frame |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
INT8 neural-network accelerator (golden model:
model/npu_model.py, NpuTop; every operation's DDR result equals the
model's bit for bit, the RTL's timing is its own). Version 1.1.0.
- Run: CMD[0] written with CTRL.EN set and no run active (CMD is
  ignored otherwise; held while the frame writer stores a frame), or
  with CTRL.AUTO after every frame the frame writer has stored. The command processor reads the 64-byte layer
  descriptors from DESC_ADDR on, starts the engine of each operation
  (word 0 [7:0]) and goes to the next one when it is done; END (0)
  finishes the run: IRQ_STATUS[0], RUNS + 1, STATUS.FRAME cleared. An
  unknown operation or a parameter the model rejects stops the run with
  IRQ_STATUS[1] (RUNS and STATUS.FRAME unchanged; the operations before
  it have written their results, as in the model).
- STATUS: [0] a run active, [1] a frame written since the last run;
  CYCLES: clocks of the last run (the RTL's own count); DET_COUNT: the
  detections of the last NMS (0 at the start of a run); irq_o = any
  IRQ_STATUS bit with its IRQ_EN bit.
- Engines: npu_elt (ADD, UPSAMPLE, COPY), npu_pool (MAXPOOL), npu_input (INPUT; the frame and
  letterbox registers taken at the start of the run), npu_conv (CONV on a PE_P x PE_O array),
  npu_decode (DECODE; the run's candidates counted for NMS), npu_nms (NMS: the detection list, DET_COUNT);
  npu_fw, the frame writer (CTRL.WRITE: the frames of s_axis to FRAME_ADDR; no frame while a run is
  active, so the buffer being read is never written). One engine at a time owns the
  DMA (npu_dma, the AXI4 master). npu_conv's output writes are posted
  (each done once sent, so the next starts without waiting for the B
  response); an operation counts as done only once every posted B is
  back, so the next one (and the CPU, after END) sees its results
  (within CONV the reads may pass its posted writes: they read other
  tensors).
Register map: src/include/npu_regs.json (npu_top.sv joins it, ID "NPU8",
to the regs port, npu_regs_if).
Parameters: ADDR_W (AXI byte address), ID_W, PE_P / PE_O (the CONV array; the results do not
depend on them).
Clock - clk (the DDR controller's). Reset - synchronous active low rst_n
(the controller's reset). Clock-domain crossings - none.

npu with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the block designs
and testbenches instantiate: the register map npu_regs (u_regs,
src/include/npu_regs.sv, ID "NPU8", VERSION and DATE at 0x00-0x08, the
registers from 0x10) and the logic npu (u_core, src/npu.sv), joined by
the register interface npu_regs_if (u_regs_if). Generated by
ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from npu_regs.json and the ports of npu:
regenerate after changing either. Clock - clk. Reset - synchronous active
low rst_n.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - npu (2026-10-26, updated for CONV 1.2.0)
// Sources:
//   [1] B. Jacob et al., "Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only
//   Inference", CVPR 2018 - INT8 x INT8 -> INT32 accumulation, per-channel requantisation by a fixed-point
//   multiplier M and a shift S, bias added in INT32
//   [2] N. P. Jouppi et al., "In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit", ISCA 2017 -
//   large INT8 MAC arrays fed from on-chip buffers, weights and activations staged from DRAM
//   [3] AMD/Xilinx, "DPUCZDX8G for Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs", PG338 - a descriptor-driven CNN engine (conv,
//   pool, element-wise, upsample) with input / output channel and pixel parallelism, DMA to DDR
//   [4] Ultralytics YOLOv8 (2023), DFL head - box sides as the expectation of a softmax over REG bins;
//   A. Neubeck, L. Van Gool, "Efficient Non-Maximum Suppression", ICPR 2006 - greedy NMS by score
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   acc = sum(w x) + b (INT32); q = clamp(round(acc M / 2^S)) [1]; MAC array with on-chip buffering [2, 3];
//   DFL: d = sum(r softmax(v)_r), softmax via exp of (max - v); greedy NMS: visit by score, suppress
//   boxes whose IoU with a kept box exceeds a limit [4].
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: INT8 / INT32 arithmetic and per-channel (M, S) requantisation with round-half-up ((acc M +
//   2^(S-1)) >> S; [1]'s rounding doubling multiply differs in rounding but the golden model defines this
//   one); an output-stationary PE_P x PE_O array (pixel x output-channel parallelism, as [3]) with weight
//   lanes and a row buffer; descriptor-driven operations on DDR; DFL decode with an exp LUT (the softmax
//   normalisation folded into the expectation's division) and the sigmoid score LUT; greedy NMS by score
//   with a same-class IoU limit, plus a cross-class limit and same-class containment (extensions of [4]:
//   one object seen as two classes, a part of a long object), the result ordered by area.
//   Simplifications (deliberate, the golden model's): one operation at a time, no layer fusion; CONV
//   overlaps its row loads (double-buffered row buffer, queued DMA reads) and output writes (output
//   buffer, posted writes) with the MACs, as the DMA engines of [2, 3] - about 14 M clocks of CONV for the
//   YOLOv8s program at 1920 x 1088 on the 64 x 64 array, within the model's estimate (CYCLES reports the
//   RTL's own); NMS sequential (O(n^2) compares, n <= CAND_MAX).
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```

### Register map (from `npu_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "NPU8" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x10 | CTRL | RW | 0 | control | EN[0] on; AUTO[1] start a run on every frame the frame writer completes; WRITE[2] frame writer on: every input frame (RGB888) to FRAME_ADDR, FRAME_STRIDE bytes per line |
| 0x14 | CMD | WO | 0 | write 1: start a run now (ignored while busy) | START[0] start |
| 0x18 | STATUS | RO | 0 | state | BUSY[0] a run in progress; FRAME[1] a frame was written since the last run started |
| 0x1C | IRQ_EN | RW | 0 | interrupt enables | DONE[0] run done; ERROR[1] bad descriptor |
| 0x20 | IRQ_STATUS | W1C | 0 | interrupt status; write 1 to clear | DONE[0] run done; ERROR[1] bad descriptor (unknown operation) |
| 0x24 | DESC_ADDR | RW | 0 | DDR address of the first layer descriptor | - |
| 0x28 | DET_ADDR | RW | 0 | DDR address of the detection list (16 bytes per detection) | - |
| 0x2C | DET_MAX | RW | 64 | most detections written | - |
| 0x30 | DET_COUNT | RO | 0 | detections written by the last run | - |
| 0x34 | FRAME_ADDR | RW | 0 | DDR address of the frame buffer (frame writer, INPUT operation) | - |
| 0x38 | FRAME_STRIDE | RW | 0 | bytes per frame buffer line | - |
| 0x3C | FRAME_SIZE | RW | 0 | frame size | WIDTH[15:0] pixels; HEIGHT[31:16] lines |
| 0x40 | LB_STEP | RW | 0 | letterbox: frame pixels per network input pixel, Q16 (bilinear scaling) | - |
| 0x44 | LB_OFFSET | RW | 0 | letterbox: top-left of the picture in the network input | X[15:0] column; Y[31:16] line |
| 0x48 | LB_SIZE | RW | 0 | letterbox: picture size in the network input | WIDTH[15:0] pixels; HEIGHT[31:16] lines |
| 0x4C | LB_INV | RW | 0 | decode: frame pixels per network input pixel, Q16 (detections in frame pixels) | - |
| 0x50 | CYCLES | RO | 0 | clocks of the last run | - |
| 0x54 | RUNS | RO | 0 | runs completed | - |
| 0x58 | LB2_STEP | RW | 0 | second letterbox (INPUT / DECODE with descriptor flag BANK2: the low-resolution pass for large objects): as LB_STEP | - |
| 0x5C | LB2_OFFSET | RW | 0 | second letterbox: as LB_OFFSET | X[15:0] column; Y[31:16] line |
| 0x60 | LB2_SIZE | RW | 0 | second letterbox: as LB_SIZE | WIDTH[15:0] pixels; HEIGHT[31:16] lines |
| 0x64 | LB2_INV | RW | 0 | second letterbox: as LB_INV | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/ai/npu/src/include/npu_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

## 8. File header

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

- The reference design has no dedicated testbench; the block is exercised inside `video_processor`. Write a self-checking testbench for it.

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh npu --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C ai/npu test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.

## 13. Report back

Files created, register map, the test list with results (with the mutation check), coverage per metric (and every waiver), synthesis resources, any change to existing IP and why, known limits.
